title: Ranveer Singh Is Making India's First ₹300 Crore Zombie Thriller. He Dropped Don for It.
excerpt: Pralay pairs him with Kalyani Priyadarshan and the son of Hansal Mehta for a post-apocalyptic survival drama that starts shooting in August.
body:
**Ranveer Singh** could have played Don. He said no.

After Dhurandhar turned him into the biggest action star in Indian cinema — ₹1,100 crore and counting for the sequel alone — the obvious move was to slide into another established franchise, keep the momentum rolling, keep the brand safe. Instead, he walked away from **Farhan Akhtar's** Don 3 and fast-tracked a zombie movie.

The film is called **Pralay**, and if even half of what's being reported holds up, it will be unlike anything Hindi cinema has attempted. A post-apocalyptic survival thriller set in a world ravaged by an outbreak, with a ₹300 crore budget, AI-driven visual effects layered onto massive physical sets, and a director who co-created one of the most celebrated shows in Indian streaming history. This is Ranveer Singh betting on himself — and betting big.

**Jai Mehta**, who co-directed *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story* alongside his father **Hansal Mehta**, is helming the project. The screenplay, co-written by Jai and **Vishal Kapoor**, is an original story — not an adaptation, despite early comparisons to José Saramago's *Blindness*. Hansal Mehta shut those down himself in an interview with *The Hollywood Reporter India*:

> "It's not an adaptation. Writers like Saramago or Salman Rushdie... I feel they are best experienced on paper. Their books lose all their magic when interpreted for cinema." — Hansal Mehta

The tone draws from the DNA of *World War Z* and *I Am Legend* — but filtered through something distinctly Indian. At its heart, Pralay is a family story. How far will a man go to protect the people he loves when the world has turned feral? The post-apocalyptic setting is the spectacle. The emotional engine is survival — intimate, desperate, human.

**Kalyani Priyadarshan** has been locked in as the female lead, marking her Hindi debut. The daughter of veteran filmmaker **Priyadarshan** and actress **Lissy**, Kalyani has already built a strong presence in South Indian cinema, including her role in the hit *Lokah*. Pairing her with Ranveer is a smart, unexpected move — she brings a rawness and physical presence that suits a survival drama far better than a more conventional Bollywood casting would.

The production is backed by **Applause Entertainment** and **True Story Films** (Hansal Mehta's banner), with Ranveer's own production house **Ma Kasam Films** also involved. Shooting is confirmed to begin in August 2026, with the production planning to blend large-scale practical sets with cutting-edge AI-generated imagery to build a dystopian India that hasn't been seen on screen before.

What makes this interesting isn't just the scale — it's the pivot. Ranveer has spent the last two years as a spy. The Dhurandhar films made him untouchable at the box office, but they also locked him into a very specific register: controlled, coiled intensity, geopolitical stakes, nationalistic undertones. Pralay asks him to do something different. It's physical, it's primal, and it's set in a genre that Indian cinema has never properly attempted at this budget level.

There have been rumours about creative differences threatening to push the project back indefinitely. But *Variety India* has confirmed the project is firmly on track, with the August floor date unchanged.

For the diaspora, this is particularly worth watching. India's genre cinema has been expanding rapidly — *Tumbbad*, *Kantara*, and the Dhurandhar films all proved that Indian audiences are hungry for world-building that extends beyond romance and family drama. Pralay is the next logical step: a big-budget, star-driven genre film that could travel internationally the way Korean genre cinema has over the past decade.

It also says something about where Bollywood's biggest stars are heading. Vicky Kaushal has blocked 18 months for *Mahavatar*, a mythological epic. Ranbir Kapoor is deep into *Ramayana*. And now Ranveer is spending the second half of 2026 inside a zombie apocalypse. The era of the quick commercial turnaround is giving way to something more ambitious — longer prep times, bigger creative swings, and the kind of singular commitment that used to be reserved for Hollywood's biggest franchises.

Pralay doesn't have a release date yet. But if it works, it won't just be a hit. It'll be a proof of concept — that Indian cinema can do apocalyptic spectacle at scale, with a homegrown star, and make the world pay attention.
